clue.text: Stake for Pennsylvania girl of French extraction

parts.note: PA is the standard abbreviation for the US state of Pennsylvania
Lisa is a girl's name
de, the French for 'of', marks origin or descent in French family names

explanation.surface: A Pennsylvania girl with French ancestry is staking a claim.
explanation.definitionFit: A palisade is a fence of pointed wooden stakes, and a single such stake can bear the name.

clue.text: A man without sex appeal, small and delicate

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside: the man goes round the appeal

parts.note: Pete is a man's name
it is old slang for sex appeal, as in the 'It girl'

explanation.surface: A man lacking allure is slight and dainty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' looks like 'lacking' but is used in its old sense of 'outside', so the man wraps the sex appeal.
explanation.definitionFit: Petite describes a woman of slight, dainty build.

clue.text: Illustrious as Chaucer's good women and Scott's Montrose

definitions.text: as Chaucer's good women and Scott's Montrose
definitions.meaning: Chaucer wrote The Legend of Good Women and Walter Scott wrote A Legend of Montrose, so both are subjects of legends

explanation.surface: Two famous literary works serve as examples of fame.
explanation.definitionFit: Something celebrated and famous is the stuff of legend, and both book titles contain the word for a traditional story.

clue.text: Posed during a film, clothed in this material?

parts.note: a model posed or sat for a portrait
in means during, as in 'in the night'
ET is Spielberg's film about an extraterrestrial

explanation.surface: An actor posing on set wears this fabric during a film.
explanation.walkthrough: 'clothed in this' is a link to the definition; the question mark admits the fanciful surface.
explanation.definitionFit: Satinet is a thin imitation satin cloth, a type of fabric.

clue.text: A number Lawrence portrayed as scum

parts.note: D is the Roman numeral for 500
Ross, the Terence Rattigan play, portrays T. E. Lawrence, who enlisted under the name Ross

explanation.surface: Lawrence of Arabia is depicted in some piece as worthless.
explanation.walkthrough: The held clue was cut short by the column break; the page shows the full text.
explanation.definitionFit: Dross is waste matter skimmed from molten metal, so worthless refuse.

clue.text: Back up new thrust in India

indicators.note: back means the little word that follows is to be read in the opposite direction

parts.note: taken as written
a jab is a quick thrust or poke

explanation.surface: A call to support a fresh push by forces in India.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Back' turns UP into PU. The definition is loose: the region named lies in India (and Pakistan).
explanation.definitionFit: Punjab is a northern state of India, so the clue's 'in India' points to a place found there.

clue.text: Peacekeepers dream anew of such a state

parts.note: UN peacekeepers are the United Nations forces

indicators.note: anew means the word dream is made over again in a new order

explanation.surface: Blue-helmeted troops imagine a fresh, weapon-free world.
explanation.walkthrough: 'anew' rearranges DREAM into ARMED.
explanation.definitionFit: Being in a condition without weapons is the state the clue describes; peacekeepers are often lightly armed.

clue.text: Never in a suit, this common fellow!

definitions.meaning: a playing card belonging to none of the four suits
a jesting, cheeky fellow, a wag

explanation.surface: A man who never wears a formal suit is just an ordinary guy.
explanation.definitionFit: The extra card in a pack has no suit, and a flippant or foolish person is a joker.

clue.text: Yeast helps to provide their livelihood

definitions.text: Yeast helps to provide their livelihood

parts.note: barm is the froth on fermenting malt liquor, a yeast
aids means helps

explanation.surface: Beer, made with yeast, gives a living to those who serve it.
explanation.walkthrough: BARM is an old word for brewer's yeast; beer made with it keeps pub staff employed.
explanation.definitionFit: Women who serve drinks in pubs earn their wages from beer, which yeast produces.

clue.text: Old squire outside northern church is a virile type

indicators.note: the virile type goes outside the other two letters

parts.note: a he-man is a strong, macho type

explanation.surface: A former attendant is a manly figure beyond a church in the north.
explanation.definitionFit: Originally the word meant a squire or page attending a great man; now it means a loyal follower.

clue.text: Whether drunk or not, he's a top-liner

definitions.text: Whether drunk or not, he's a top-liner

parts.words: Whether drunk or not, he's a top-liner
parts.note: tight is slang for drunk, and a performer who walks along a high rope is literally on a line at the top, whether or not he has been drinking

explanation.surface: A star performer, sober or tipsy, still heads the bill.
explanation.definitionFit: A circus artiste balancing on a taut high cable works on a line high up, and 'tight' doubles as slang for intoxicated.

clue.text: A number of workers are in occupation

definitions.note: the definition describes people who occupy a property, so a phrase stands for a plural noun

parts.note: ten is a number
worker ants are the classic crossword workers

explanation.surface: Many employees are busy at their jobs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'occupation' suggests jobs, fitting 'workers', but here it means occupying a home; 'are' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Tenants are the people who occupy rented premises, living there under a lease.

clue.text: County court has medical graduate confined

indicators.note: the court is said to hold the graduate shut up inside it
the court is said to hold the graduate shut up inside it

parts.note: a curia is a court, especially the papal court or a Roman law court
MB, Bachelor of Medicine, is a medical degree

explanation.surface: A provincial court is holding a newly qualified doctor in custody.
explanation.walkthrough: CUMBRIA is a county in north-west England, home of the Lake District.
explanation.definitionFit: Cumbria is an English administrative area of the kind called a county, in the north-west of the country.

clue.text: Crazy act of mutt, endlessly being the dog's-body

indicators.note: crazy says the letters that follow are thrown into wild disorder

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: endlessly says the dog word loses its final letter

explanation.surface: A mongrel behaves madly while being the household drudge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endlessly' cuts MUTT to MUT; 'Crazy' rearranges ACTOF plus MUT into the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A factotum is a servant who does every kind of job, just like a dogsbody who gets all the menial work.

clue.text: Archer may be late — he's such a gossip!

parts.note: William Tell is the legendary Swiss archer

indicators.note: may be says the word late could be rearranged into another form

explanation.surface: An archer is warned he might be tardy, and he blabs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'may be' rearranges LATE into TALE.
explanation.definitionFit: A telltale reports others' secrets or misdeeds, a tattler.

clue.text: Deceived theologian about university exercises

indicators.note: the theologian goes round the other letters

parts.note: DD, Doctor of Divinity, is a theology degree, so a theologian
PE is physical education, school exercises

explanation.surface: A divine was taken in over college workouts.
explanation.definitionFit: To be duped is to be tricked or fooled by someone.

clue.text: The average quantity is most important

parts.note: par is the normal or average level
an amount is a quantity

explanation.surface: Typical quantity is what matters above all.
explanation.definitionFit: Paramount means supreme, of chief importance.

clue.text: Wren slid badly, becoming a rook

indicators.note: badly says the letters of wren slid fall into disorder

explanation.surface: A small songbird stumbled and turned into a larger black bird.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rook' looks like a bird beside 'Wren', but here it means a cheat.
explanation.definitionFit: To rook someone is to cheat them, so a rook is a cheat or fraudster.

clue.text: He is said to have a luxurious-life. — ironically

indicators.note: is said marks the name as heard rather than spelt

parts.note: the man in the phrase 'the life of Riley', proverbial for luxurious ease

explanation.surface: A man reputed to live in comfort is described with gentle irony.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to have a luxurious life' tells you which 'He' is meant: Riley, of the idiom 'living the life of Riley'.
explanation.definitionFit: Speaking wryly means with dry, mocking humour, which is what speaking ironically conveys.

clue.text: Lifted up grassland plant, uttering loud-cries

indicators.note: in a down clue lifted up means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: a ley is land temporarily under grass
ling is heather

explanation.surface: A meadow plant was pulled up while someone shouted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lifted up' turns LEY into YEL.
explanation.definitionFit: Yelling means shouting or screaming loudly.

clue.text: Touch down by target — the Eiffel Tower, possibly

indicators.note: by means next to, so the second piece sits beside the first

parts.note: an aircraft touching down is landing
a mark is a target, as in 'hit the mark'

explanation.surface: A plane lands near its objective, with the Paris tower in view.
explanation.definitionFit: The Paris tower is a famous example of a prominent structure that identifies a place.

clue.text: Extracts money from Central European weakling

parts.note: to milk is to drain money out of someone

indicators.note: central means the middle letters of the next word

explanation.surface: Someone fleeces a feeble person from the heart of Europe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Central' takes the middle pair of EUROPEAN, OP.
explanation.definitionFit: A milksop is a feeble, timid person lacking courage.

clue.text: Liberal support for museum he wrecked

indicators.note: in a down clue the support goes beneath the museum

parts.note: the V and A is London's Victoria and Albert Museum

explanation.surface: A Liberal backer for a gallery he destroyed.
explanation.walkthrough: The V and A is the Victoria and Albert Museum in London; 'he wrecked' defines one who wrecks.
explanation.definitionFit: A vandal is a person who deliberately damages property.

clue.text: Obstruction beside the isthmus? At least it's ornamental

indicators.note: beside places the two pieces next to each other

parts.note: a neck of land is a narrow strip joining two larger areas, an isthmus
a let is a hindrance, as in 'without let or hindrance'

explanation.surface: A blockage next to a land bridge is at least decorative.
explanation.walkthrough: 'At least' is a link; the obstruction is LET in the old sense of hindrance, also the tennis call.
explanation.definitionFit: A necklet is a decorative band or chain worn round the throat, purely for adornment.

clue.text: Figures a civil servant revealed

indicators.note: revealed means the abbreviation is opened up to show something inside it

parts.note: CS is the Civil Service
one means a, a single

explanation.surface: Numbers produced by an official are disclosed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'revealed' is an unusual container signal: the abbreviation is opened up to show a word inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Cones are solid figures in geometry.

clue.text: Problem created by woman rejecting hat at the outset

indicators.note: rejecting means the hat word is turned back on itself

parts.note: lid is slang for a hat, and it comes at the outset of the answer
Emma is a woman's name

explanation.surface: A woman refusing a hat from the start creates difficulty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rejecting' means sending back, so the hat word is turned round before the woman follows it.
explanation.definitionFit: A dilemma is a predicament forcing a hard choice, a kind of awkward situation.

clue.text: This dog takes some boarding out!

indicators.note: some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: This dog needs some kennel time away from home.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft definition 'This dog takes' wrongly included 'takes', which is a link word, so the definition is just 'This dog'.
explanation.definitionFit: The dingo is Australia's wild dog.

clue.text: Man possibly surrounded by protracted noise in the Atlantic

indicators.note: the island is placed inside the two-word noise phrase

parts.note: protracted means drawn out, long
a sound is a noise
the Isle of Man is an example of an island

explanation.surface: Perhaps a man is engulfed by prolonged din out at sea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Man' is the Isle of Man. The definition is loose: the strait lies off the Atlantic coast of New York.
explanation.definitionFit: This strait is an arm of the ocean between Connecticut and the New York island of the same name.

clue.text: Note evidence and quit

parts.note: re is the second note of the sol-fa scale
a sign is an indication or evidence

explanation.surface: Someone notes the proof and walks out of the job.
explanation.definitionFit: To resign is to give up a post, which is to quit it.

clue.text: Damaged a hip? Lots are mended here

definitions.text: Damaged a hip? Lots are mended here

indicators.note: damaged says the letters of the next words are knocked out of shape

explanation.surface: Injured your hip? Plenty of people get fixed up in this place.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Damaged' rearranges A HIP plus LOTS; the whole clue also describes the place.
explanation.definitionFit: A hospital is where patients, including those with broken hips, are treated and repaired.
